items.title: StrataFlux: Memory-Hierarchy-Native Low-Bit LLM Inference
items.summary: Quantization reduces the memory and bandwidth demands of large language model (LLM) inference but can degrade accuracy; offloading higher-precision data can instead stall generation. We introduce StrataFlux, a framework that challenges this tradeoff by recovering accuracy lost to low-bit weight and key-value (KV) cache quantization while retaining quantization's memory and speed advantages. StrataFlux co-designs refinement representation, selection, and delivery to make host RAM and solid-state drives useful source

items.title: ROCm InferaSim: Cut LLM Serving Trial Costs and Deploy the Best Configuration
items.summary: Serving an LLM well means making a lot of choices before you know the answer. You pick an engine, a parallel layout, precisions and scheduler settings, and for disaggregated serving a split between prefill and decode. That leaves thousands of candidates, and each trial ties up one or more multi-GPU nodes for minutes. Measuring every candidate in our searches would take about 25,000 GPU-hours, so most teams try a few guesses and keep the best. A guess that misses costs you extra GPUs or a missed latency target.

items.title: PrimusClaw: An Open-Source Managed Agent Runtime for AMD Instinct GPU Clusters
items.summary: PrimusClaw is an open-source managed agent runtime: a session store, an agent harness, and per-session sandboxes that you run in your own Kubernetes cluster, next to your AMD Instinct™ GPUs. In production use at AMD since April 2026, two PrimusClaw deployments have hosted more than 40,000 agent sessions for more than 70 users: over 100,000 agent-hours, more than 4 million tool calls, and more than 500 billion prompt tokens. On the main deployment, the median run lasted 3.4 hours (Endnote 2).
